candidates.change_summary: Change return value from true to false.

Change return value to a bool constant true literal (same as original) is NOT distinct — skipped. Instead, replace return true with return !true; (i.e., false). Already covered. Move on. Replace return true with return _s; — but _s is out of scope. Replace return true with require(false) — but that would revert, breaking the requirement that both complete. Replace return true with return !false; still true. No distinct new value. Next: delete the require inside the call success check, so the call can fail silently. This changes behavior when call fails — it would not revert but return true. However, target says both complete (do not revert) and return different values. If a call fails in original, it reverts; in mutant, it completes and returns true. So that qualifies.

Remove the require(_s) check — already covered by delete of require(_s) block. Instead, move the return true inside the loop after the call but before the loop continues, so it returns after first iteration. This changes behavior when _tos.length > 1: original processes all addresses, mutant returns after first address.
Require each external call's success flag to be false instead of true.
Replace the transferFrom selector id with the transfer selector, causing each call to invoke a different function on caddress.
Delete the require(_tos.length > 0) guard so an empty _tos array no longer reverts and the function can return true.
Initialize the loop index to 1 instead of 0, skipping the first recipient in _tos.
Change the loop condition to i <= _tos.length, causing an out-of-bounds access for i == _tos.length.
Replace the post-increment i++ with i += 2, thereby skipping every other recipient call.
Swap from and _tos[i] in the encodeWithSelector arguments, changing which address is the spender and which is the recipient.
Change the amount argument in the external call from v to 0, causing zero-value transfers.
Change the require(_s) to require(!_s), reverting when the external call succeeds and passing when it fails.
Change the final return value from true to false.
Remove the require that enforces a non-empty recipient array, allowing zero-recipient calls to succeed instead of reverting.
Replace the loop condition so it never executes, making transfer return true without making any external calls.
Remove the require on the external call success flag, so a failed transferFrom call no longer causes transfer to revert.
Change the return value from true to false, altering the observable success value of a completed transfer call.
